summary: Standing Kootenai National Forest lookout in Lincoln County, Montana; 1921 tree platform, 1934 L-4 pole tower, steel tower moved here in 1984; NHLR-registered 2021.

facts.design: Present steel tower (type not stated); 1934 predecessor was a 40 ft pole L-4 tower
facts.agency: US Forest Service; Kootenai National Forest and Montana DNRC also credited

events.note: First lookout structure: a crow's nest tree platform, still standing about 1/8 mile south of the present lookout; platform has fallen down
40 ft pole L-4 tower built on the middle of three summits
Present steel tower moved here from Johnson Peak near Whitefish
Registered January 9, 2021 as US 1507, MT 85; nominated by Kyle Stetler

evidence.supports: Kootenai NF, Lincoln County, Montana location
first structure a crow's nest tree platform built in 1921
evidence.quote: a crow's nest tree platform, built in 1921

evidence.supports: 1934 40 ft pole L-4 tower on middle of three summits
evidence.quote: In 1934, a 40' pole L-4 tower was built on the middle of 3 summits.

evidence.supports: present steel tower moved in 1984 from Johnson Peak near Whitefish
evidence.quote: In 1984, the present steel tower was moved from Johnson Peak near Whitefish.
The lookout has been staffed in recent years.

evidence.supports: elevation 6480 ft on firelookout.com, differs from NHLR

evidence.quote: was moved from Johnson Peak near Whitefish.

corrections.proposed: 1921 built: crow's nest tree platform, not the present tower; present steel tower moved here in 1984
corrections.why: Both pages describe the 1921 structure as a tree platform used as a crow's nest, and say the present steel tower came from Johnson Peak in 1984.

corrections.proposed: Present steel tower (type not stated); 1934 predecessor was a 40 ft pole L-4 tower
corrections.why: L-4 describes the 1934 pole tower that was apparently destroyed in 1974, not the present steel tower.

corrections.proposed: remove; no height is given for the present steel tower
corrections.why: 40 ft (12.2 m) is the height of the 1934 pole tower, not the present steel tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 6,489 ft (1,978 m); firelookout.com gives 6480 ft. The record keeps the Register figure (1977.8 m). Not checked on the ground.
NHLR says administered by US Forest Service; firelookout.com credits Kootenai National Forest/DNRC. Both are listed in facts.agency.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1921 'built' and L-4 design/12.2 m height describe earlier structures, not the present steel tower, so corrections are proposed. Build date and design of the 1984 steel tower are not given by any source read. No access or visitor information found; a WebSearch for rental or visiting returned nothing for Calx (Big Creek Baldy and Yaak Mountain results were for other towers and were not used). Staffing has no year.
